Photograph: Neil Hall/EPA UK news Rubio says foreign actor was ‘clearly’ behind suspected RAF Fairford bomb plot The US secretary of state offered no evidence for his claims, and also said many people were ‘disturbed’ that the five suspects had been released on bail Guardian staff and agencies Mon 28 Sep 2026 23.29 EDT Last modified on Mon 28 Sep 2026 23.32 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said unequivocally that a foreign actor was involved in the suspected UK bomb plot at RAF Fairford, hours after the five suspects arrested close to the airbase were released on bail. “What could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a ‌very serious situation,” Rubio said in an interview with Fox News on Monday evening, adding that it “clearly involves the hands ‌of a foreign actor.” Rubio provided no evidence for his claims. Questions remain over Iran’s link to alleged RAF Fairford bomb plot Read more The five men, all British nationals from London in their early 20s , were ⁠detained early on Sunday after police ⁠were alerted by a local farmer about three ​white vans driving towards RAF Fairford, a British base that houses US bombers that fly missions against Iran. They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and preparing an act of terrorism, with an Iranian link a key line of inquiry. Their release on police bail suggests detectives believe it is unlikely they were on the brink of a mass casualty attack by exploding a bomb close to the base, sources said. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said in July the base was a legitimate target. Iran’s embassy in London has denied any involvement in the events near RAF Fairford. While thanking the British authorities for their handling of the incident, Rubio also said a lot of people were “disturbed that some of these people [being investigated] have been released on bail”. 8:29 Who is behind suspected bomb plot at RAF base? - The Latest Earlier in the day, Donald Trump told reporters at the White House on Monday that he would not have released the suspects on bail. “We know everything about them. We would not have released them.” Asked whether the case was linked to Iran, Trump said: “It might be.” Pressed to give details, Trump said: “I’d rather not. I mean I know the answer, I could be very specific, but I’d rather not say. I would not have released them.” Trump has previously suggested the plot was known to the US authorities, but British sources suggested the specific activities of the men were unknown. The head of UK counter-terrorism policing, the assistant commissioner Laurence Taylor, said the release of the men on bail did not mean the investigation was over and that they were subject to “stringent conditions”. He said: “I know there is significant interest in whether the current geopolitical context has a bearing on this incident. At counter-terrorism policing we are working within this context every day, and at this stage we are keeping an open mind in this investigation. Emergency teams deploy bomb disposal robot at RAF Fairford air base “… But be assured, we are considering this from every possible angle. Including, that this may be activity committed by proxies, or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly working on behalf of a foreign state.” An initial examination of the vans led police to suspect they carried explosive materials, with assessments made as to whether they were viable improvised explosive devices. After the suspects’ release it emerged that no explosive material had been found. Iran is suspected of using proxies in the UK, in incidents ranging from alleged arson attacks against Jewish targets to men flying a basic drone near the Israeli embassy. Photograph: Andrew Toth/FilmMagic US news Kyle Kennedy, granddaughter of Robert F Kennedy, dies aged 42 Kennedy taught in New York public schools and advocated for disability rights after suffering severe spinal cord injury Lucy Campbell Tue 20 Oct 2026 16.55 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 16.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Kyle Kennedy, the granddaughter of Robert F Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy, has died at the age of 42. Kyle, the daughter of Michael Kennedy, who died in 1997, and Victoria Gifford Kennedy, “passed away peacefully” on 21 September at her home in Westwood, Massachusetts, according to her obituary published by Burke Funeral Homes. Her cause of death is pending, the Westwood town clerk told the Guardian. View image in fullscreen Kyle Kennedy speaks during the 2019 Robert F Kennedy Human Rights Ripple Of Hope Awards in 2018 in New York. Photograph: Michael Loccisano/Getty Images for Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Born on 6 July 1984 in Washington DC, Kyle Kennedy spent much of her upbringing in Cohasset, Massachusetts , before pursuing a career as an educator. Her obituary noted she was dedicated to early childhood education and worked on educational reform for disadvantaged children and later advocated for people living with disabilities. She taught in public schools in New York City in the program Teach for America after graduating college, where she had earned a bachelor’s degree in history from Georgetown University, a master of science in early education from Pace University, and a master of education in education policy and management from the Harvard Graduate School of Education. In August 2012, she married Liam Kerr in Boston, with whom she had three children – Conor, Josie and Declan. The obituary refers to Kerr as Kyle’s “former husband”. An avid sports player and long-distance runner, Kyle ran the 2019 Boston Marathon in a “driving rainstorm”, finishing the race 20 minutes faster than her father. A year later, she suffered a severe spinal cord injury that “resulted in long term paralysis, disability, and other medical challenges”. Per her obituary, her final years “brought struggles but Kyle fought to maintain her dry wit and determination through it all, trying to be the best possible mother to her sons”. In this time, she began advocating for people with disabilities, “including testifying at the Massachusetts state house in a hearing on discrimination in disabled health care”. Kyle is survived by her sons, Conor, 12, and Declan, 10; her former husband, Liam; her mother, Victoria; her brother Michael; sister Rory; and her nieces and nephews McKie, Quinn, Jack and Caleb. The funeral service was held privately.
